description: Born in New Orleans, jazz mixed African rhythms, blues and European harmony, then invented swing, bebop and modal jazz.

hero.hook: In a port city, America invents its classical music: jazz.

blocks.text: Jazz was born in  towards the end of the 19th century. Port of Louisiana, French, Spanish, African and Caribbean crossroads, the city is a sound laboratory. [[New Orleans]]

Born in the violence of slavery and segregation, this music became the “classical music of America”. Over the course of a century, it has influenced rock, funk and hip-hop. To understand jazz is to understand a freedom invented under constraint.

At the end of the 19th century, New Orleans mixed Creoles of color, descendants of enslaved Africans, and European immigrants. European opera and Caribbean rhythms intersect there. At , the only place in the North where black populations had the right to meet on Sundays, drums and African polyrhythms survive. [[Congo Square in New Orleans]]

blocks.caption: Congo Square: African rhythmic memory in the heart of Louisiana.

blocks.text: The **brass bands** (brass bands) liven up parades and funerals: slow march towards the cemetery, explosion of joy on the return. This shift between mourning and celebration is the emotional soul of emerging jazz.
The pioneer **Buddy Bolden**, a barber by trade, has never been recorded: his legend rests with those who heard his cornet from across the Mississippi.

Jazz inherits from the blues its , “inflected” notes which create expressive tension. From gospel and work songs, he draws the call-and-response. These elements are placed on the European harmony of brass bands. [[blue notes]]

The break is : the partition is no longer a law, but a grid. The musician composes in real time. In an America of , this freedom is also political: asserting one's singularity when the system wants to erase it. [[Improvisation in jazz]] [[Jim Crow laws]]
In 1917, the first jazz record was recorded by white musicians (Original Dixieland Jass Band): record companies did not yet dare to bet on black inventors of the genre.

sections.title: Blue notes, improvisation and Jim Crow

blocks.text: With the  to Chicago and New York, jazz left the South. **Louis Armstrong** places the virtuoso soloist at the center. In Harlem, during the , jazz was celebrated as black modernity. In the 1930s,  by **Duke Ellington** made America dance. [[Great Migration]] [[Harlem Renaissance]] [[swing]]

blocks.caption: Louis Armstrong: the soloist becomes the heart of jazz.

blocks.text: After 1945, **Charlie Parker** invented : fast tempos, complex harmonies, listening music. In **1959**, **Miles Davis** released *Kind of Blue*: the  slows down chord changes to explore a color. It is still the best-selling jazz record in the world. [[bebop]] [[modal jazz]]

blocks.caption: Kind of Blue (1959): modal, calm and revolutionary jazz.

blocks.text: The New York club Birdland takes its name from Parker's nickname, "Bird". Parker himself was kicked out one night after an argument.

sections.title: Armstrong, swing, bebop, Kind of Blue

blocks.text: In the 1960s, the  broke the framework, linked to civil rights. Then the  crosses electric rock and funk. Swing, this elastic pulsation, still irrigates rock and hip-hop. Institutionalized in conservatories, jazz remains a language of the moment: each concert is unique. [[free jazz]] [[jazz fusion]]
